Day-to-day care

Maintaining Your Unit

Garbage Disposals

Food scraps, bones, popcorn, peels, and other hard items should never go into a disposal. Only soft, liquid, and/or biodegradable foods should be inserted.

Clear drains are key to a well-functioning home. Avoid putting grease, coffee grounds, and hair down sinks and showers. Simple habits like routine hot-water rinses help prevent buildup and extend the life of your plumbing.

Full disposal care guide

Fridges & Freezers

Refrigerators and freezers must not be overfilled. Overstuffing causes food spoilage and can lead to unit failure. Leave space toward the back of the freezer for air circulation.

Door Locks & Codes

Your entry door uses a 3-point locking system. See how to lock and unlock it.

Bedroom and bathroom doors do not have coded or keyed locks. Lone Mountain Property Management will not provide or upgrade door lock systems.

Smoke Alarms

Smoke alarms chirp when the battery needs to be replaced. You do not need to remove the unit to change the battery; the compartment is on the side of the unit.

Smoke alarms may never be covered or removed. Tampering with a smoke detector will result in a $500 fine.

Summer Cooling

Gateway Village units, like all of our other housing locations, do not have central air or A/C. To help manage the heat, we recommend:

  • Night cooling: keep windows open at night and use fans to bring in cooler air.
  • Daytime blocking: from about 10 AM to 8 PM, keep blinds and windows closed to block out heat and sun.
  • Extra cooling tools: many residents buy a floor fan or an evaporative cooler, which can make a noticeable difference.

We are happy to provide a fan if you need one. Just let us know and we will get one to you as soon as possible.

Your entry door

3-Point Door Lock System

A 3-point lock locks in three places at the same time instead of one. A regular lock is one strong arm holding the door. A 3-point lock is three strong arms (top, middle, and bottom). It makes the door extra secure and keeps it from wobbling.

How to unlock the door

  1. Put the key in the lock.
  2. Turn the key slowly (usually toward the door frame).
  3. You might hear three little clicks. That is the top, middle, and bottom unlocking.
  4. Push the handle down.
  5. Open the door.

If the key feels hard to turn, gently lift the handle up a tiny bit while turning the key.

How to lock the door

  1. Close the door completely.
  2. Lift the handle up firmly. This sends the top and bottom locks into place.
  3. Put the key in.
  4. Turn the key until it stops.
  5. Remove the key.

Now all three locks are holding the door tight.

How to open the door (from inside)

  1. Make sure it is unlocked.
  2. Push the handle down.
  3. Pull or push the door open.

That is it!

How to close the door

  1. Gently push the door shut until it clicks.
  2. Make sure it is fully closed (no gap).

The middle part usually clicks automatically, but the top and bottom are not locked yet. Follow the steps above to lock the door.

Easy way to remember

  • Handle down = open
  • Handle up = get ready to lock
  • Turn key = lock or unlock all three spots

Important tips

  • Never slam the door.
  • Always lift the handle before turning the key to lock.

Lost keys: a missing mail key is $25, and a missing unit key is up to $350 because the lock needs to be re-keyed.

Protecting your unit

Kitchen Disposal Use & Care

Improper use of the kitchen disposal, sink drains, and toilets can cause serious plumbing damage and costly repairs. Residents are responsible for using these systems properly. The disposal is designed to handle small amounts of soft food waste only, not bulk food scraps.

Keep it working

  • Scrape food scraps from plates into the garbage before rinsing.
  • During food prep, place most food waste directly into the garbage.
  • Never put paper, plastic, metal, or any non-food items in the disposal.

Never put these in the disposal:

  • Meat scraps or bones
  • Popcorn
  • Raw hard vegetables
  • Fruit rinds
  • Potato peels
  • Whole food items

Proper disposal operation

  1. Make sure the disposal is clear of debris before use.
  2. Do not pack food into the disposal.
  3. Turn on cold water and let it run.
  4. Flip the disposal switch to process small amounts of food waste.
  5. Let the water run briefly after turning the disposal off to flush the drain.

Important reminder

Disposals are meant to handle minimal leftover food waste. They do not replace the garbage can.

Improper use may result in maintenance charges if damage occurs due to misuse.

Keep it clean

Garbage & Recycling

Pickup day

Garbage is picked up every Wednesday morning.

  • Put your cans at the curb by 7:00 AM on pickup day.
  • Return them to the parking lot by the end of the day.

Placing your cans

Leave at least one foot between cans so the truck’s mechanical arms can reach in and grab each one.

Cans will not be picked up if the driver cannot reasonably pull up next to them.

Extra trash & large items

  • One extra bag outside the cart is allowed per month. After that, there is a minimum charge of $5.00 per bag.
  • Larger items are charged at a higher rate. Please contact the housing team before putting them out.

Trash that does not fit in the containers is not the responsibility of the Landlord or Property Manager, and all removal costs are the responsibility of the tenant.

Recycling

A variety of recycling options are available at the Gallatin Gateway Community Center.

Please do not place garbage in the recycling bin. Help keep the property clean and litter-free.

Get a parking pass

Gateway Village Parking

If you have a vehicle in the parking lot, please fill out the parking pass application so your vehicle is not ticketed, towed, or booted. After you submit it, we will reach out to schedule a good time to drop off or pick up your pass. Place the pass on the upper left or right of your front windshield.

Parking pass application

When a registered vehicle can still be ticketed or towed

Registered resident vehicles will not be ticketed or towed unless the vehicle:

  • Is parked in a space reserved for disability parking only
  • Is parked in a no parking zone
  • Is parked in a fire lane
  • Is blocking access to the trash receptacles or dumpsters
  • Is clearly disabled and has broken parts, glass, or flat tires

Penalties

  • First offense: warning
  • Second offense: $10.00
  • Third offense: $50.00
  • Fourth offense and all offenses after: $100.00 per offense

Any repeat offense, more than three (3) ticketed offenses in any one week, or more than ten (10) ticketed offenses in any consecutive eight (8) week period, will result in immediate disablement of the vehicle by booting or other appropriate means and/or towing and impoundment. The fine for release of any booted or impounded vehicle is $500.00 per offense. The property manager may also determine other special purposes from time to time.

All offenses are evidenced by a ticket issued by an authorized Property Manager. The fine is due and payable, in cash, at the office of Property Management within five (5) days after the ticket is issued. A record of all offenses, including the name and address of the offender, the license plate number of the vehicle involved, sanctions levied, and fines paid, is kept and maintained by Lone Mountain Property Management.
